# 什么是 GPTBot？

- 原标题：What Is GPTBot?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-14
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/gptbot/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

GPTBot 是 OpenAI 于 2023 年 8 月推出的网络爬虫，用于收集公开可用的网页内容，帮助训练其生成式 AI 模型。它通过 GPTBot 用户代理标识自己的身份，并遵守 robots.txt。屏蔽 GPTBot 可以让网站退出模型训练，但不会阻止 ChatGPT 的实时浏览，也不会让网站从其搜索结果中消失。

### 关键要点

- GPTBot 是 OpenAI 的**三种**代理之一。GPTBot 用于训练模型，OAI-SearchBot 构建 ChatGPT 搜索索引，ChatGPT-User 则抓取用户要求 ChatGPT 阅读的页面。屏蔽其中一种并不会屏蔽其他代理。
- GPTBot 遵守 robots.txt。使用 `User-agent: GPTBot`／`Disallow: /` 规则，可以让内容不被纳入未来的训练，但不会影响 ChatGPT 能否在实时答案中引用你。
- OpenAI 为每种代理公布了可核验的 IP 范围（`openai.com/gptbot.json`、`searchbot.json`、`chatgpt-user.json`），因此可以确认请求是否真实，而非伪造用户代理。
- 屏蔽 GPTBot 是有关训练数据的决策，不是有关可见度的决策。如果你希望获得 AI 引用，应保持 OAI-SearchBot 不被屏蔽。

### GPTBot 如何运作

GPTBot 是 OpenAI 用来从开放网络收集公开文本的[自动化爬虫](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/)，这些内容可能被用于训练未来的 GPT 模型。OpenAI 在 2023 年 8 月推出它时，也提供了文档，明确告诉站长如何控制它。从机制上看，它与遵守规范的搜索爬虫一样：通过 HTTP 请求页面，以独立的用户代理标明身份，并在抓取前读取网站的 robots.txt。

用户代理是识别它的关键。GPTBot 请求携带的标识中包含字符串 `GPTBot`，以及指向 `https://openai.com/gptbot` 的网址，例如：`Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot`。由于用户代理可以被伪造，OpenAI 还在 `openai.com/gptbot.json` 公布爬虫的 IP 范围，让服务器能确认声称来自 GPTBot 的请求是否确实源于 OpenAI 的基础设施。

GPTBot *不会*做的两件事需要说清楚，因为大多数误解都出在这里。GPTBot 不会为了回答用户当前的问题而抓取页面，也不会构建 ChatGPT 用来搜索的索引。它唯一的工作是收集可能用于训练模型的内容。正因为用途单一，针对 GPTBot 的 robots.txt 规则会改变未来模型能否从你的内容中学习，却不会改变当前 ChatGPT 检索和引用你的方式。如果你想影响的是 AI 系统能够检索什么，而不是用什么来训练，那么你关注的是另一个层次，也就是 [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) 文件以及保持面向检索的代理畅通所涉及的层次。

### GPTBot、OAI-SearchBot 与 ChatGPT-User 的对比

OpenAI 运行三种独立的代理，各自有自己的用户代理标识、用途和 robots.txt 控制方式。屏蔽其中一种并不等于屏蔽全部。这是理解 GPTBot 时最重要的一点。

| 代理 | 用途 | 用户代理标识 | robots.txt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **GPTBot** | 收集内容以训练 OpenAI 模型 | `GPTBot` | 遵守；屏蔽即可退出训练 |
| **OAI-SearchBot** | 构建 ChatGPT 搜索和引用所依赖的索引 | `OAI-SearchBot` | 遵守；允许访问才能继续在 ChatGPT 中被引用 |
| **ChatGPT-User** | 用户要求 ChatGPT 阅读具体页面时抓取该页面 | `ChatGPT-User` | 由用户发起，不属于自动化爬取 |

实际影响是：如果你希望阻止内容用于训练模型，同时继续出现在 ChatGPT 的答案中，就应屏蔽 GPTBot、允许 OAI-SearchBot。如果你把名称里带有“bot”的代理全部屏蔽，也会把自己移出为实时答案提供内容的搜索索引，这与大多数发布者真正想要的结果相反。ChatGPT-User 又是另一回事：只有人在聊天中粘贴网址，或明确要求 ChatGPT 打开页面时，它才会触发。因此，OpenAI 将其视为用户操作，而不是决定网站是否具备搜索资格的爬取。

### 如何允许或屏蔽 GPTBot

GPTBot 遵守机器人排除协议，因此可以通过网站根目录下的 `robots.txt` 文件进行控制。要完全屏蔽 GPTBot，加入：

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /
```

如果只想禁止 GPTBot 访问网站的一部分，例如会员区和结账流程，则只禁止这些路径：

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /members/
Disallow: /checkout/
```

要明确允许它，可以不写任何 GPTBot 规则（默认允许），也可以直接声明：

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /
```

关键细节是，每种代理都必须单独指明。屏蔽 `GPTBot` 的规则不会对 `OAI-SearchBot` 或 `ChatGPT-User` 作出规定。如果你想退出训练，但继续出现在 ChatGPT 搜索结果里，文件中就需要两组独立规则：一组禁止 GPTBot，另一组允许 OAI-SearchBot。修改后需要留出一定生效时间；OpenAI 提醒，robots.txt 的变更可能需要大约一天才会在其系统中反映出来。

### GPTBot 示例

设想一家中型旅游内容网站，看到关于 AI 抓取的新闻后，决定“屏蔽 AI 机器人”。工程师添加了一条宽泛规则，禁止用户代理中包含“GPT”的所有请求，认为这样就能一次拦住 OpenAI 的爬虫。来自 GPTBot 的训练抓取流量确实降到了零，符合预期。

三个月后，营销团队发现，这个网站从 ChatGPT 的引用来源中消失了，而这些目的地指南领域过去本是它的优势。现在 ChatGPT 引用的是竞争对手。原因不是排名变化，也不是内容问题，而是 robots.txt 规则。过于宽泛的屏蔽还匹配到了负责 ChatGPT 搜索索引的 `OAI-SearchBot`，因此发布者悄悄把自己从提供实时引用的系统中移除了。

解决方法是分开处理这两种意图。发布者重写 robots.txt，明确屏蔽 GPTBot，以退出训练；明确允许 OAI-SearchBot，以重新获得搜索可见度。随后通过服务器日志，把请求 IP 与 OpenAI 公布的 IP 范围交叉核对，确认 OAI-SearchBot 再次抓取这些指南。几周内，目的地页面重新进入 ChatGPT 的引用来源，而退出训练的设置仍然有效。

### 人们容易弄错的一点

我最常见到的错误，是团队因为某篇博客说要“把 AI 挡在外面”，就把“屏蔽 GPTBot”的规则粘进 robots.txt，几个月后却又纳闷为什么自己从 ChatGPT 的引用来源里消失了。这其实是两扇不同的门。GPTBot 决定你的文字是否帮助训练下一代模型；OAI-SearchBot 决定 ChatGPT *今天*能否找到并引用你。屏蔽 GPTBot，只是在退出训练，对付费档案库或专有研究来说，这完全是可以理解的选择。但如果同一条规则不小心也挡住了 OAI-SearchBot，你就悄悄把自己从支撑实时答案的搜索索引中删除了。逐个代理检查你的 robots.txt。“AI 爬虫”不是一种单一的东西，一行规则也控制不了全部。

这里的要点是：GPTBot 是一个针对具体用途的控制对象，而不是总管所有 AI 的开关。它只回答一个问题——*OpenAI 可以用这些内容训练模型吗？* 至于 AI 系统如何发现、读取和引用你的页面，其他每一个问题都由名称不同的其他代理负责。分别管理它们，用 IP 范围核验请求，并单独评估是否允许训练，而不要把这个问题与自己大概率希望保留的可见度捆在一起。

### 常见问题

#### 屏蔽 GPTBot 会让我的网站从 ChatGPT 中消失吗？

不会。GPTBot 只负责收集训练数据。ChatGPT 的实时答案依赖 OAI-SearchBot（搜索索引）和 ChatGPT-User（用户触发的抓取）。如果想退出训练又保持在 ChatGPT 中的可见度，应屏蔽 GPTBot，但允许 OAI-SearchBot。

#### GPTBot 的用户代理字符串是什么？

GPTBot 会使用包含 GPTBot 标识和网址 [https://openai.com/gptbot](https://openai.com/gptbot) 的用户代理来标明身份，例如 `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot`。OpenAI 还会在 [openai.com/gptbot.json](http://openai.com/gptbot.json) 公布其 IP 范围，供核验使用。

#### 如何屏蔽 GPTBot？

在网站根目录的 robots.txt 中加入两行：先写 `User-agent: GPTBot`，再写 `Disallow: /`。GPTBot 遵守 robots.txt，因此这会阻止它为训练收集你的内容。如果只想屏蔽网站的一部分，则改为禁止具体路径。

#### GPTBot 遵守 robots.txt 吗？

遵守。GPTBot 会遵循 robots.txt 指令，OpenAI 也提供了如何允许或禁止它的文档。请注意，用户明确要求 ChatGPT 阅读某个页面时进行抓取的 ChatGPT-User，是由用户发起的操作，不被视为自动化爬取。

### 核心结论

GPTBot 是 OpenAI 三种代理中负责训练抓取的那一种。把它当作“AI”的单一总开关，正是网站意外让自己从 ChatGPT 中消失的原因。应分别决定训练和可见度这两个问题：如果不希望内容进入未来模型，就屏蔽 GPTBot；如果希望在 AI 答案中被引用，就保持 OAI-SearchBot 畅通。在 robots.txt 中按每种代理的独立名称管理，并对照 OpenAI 公布的 IP 范围核验流量。

## 英文原文

GPTBot is OpenAI’s web crawler, introduced in August 2023, that collects publicly available web content to help train its generative AI models. It identifies itself with the GPTBot user-agent and obeys robots.txt. Blocking GPTBot opts a site out of model training but does not stop ChatGPT’s live browsing or its search results.

### Key Takeaways

- GPTBot is one of **three** OpenAI agents. GPTBot trains models, OAI-SearchBot builds the ChatGPT search index, and ChatGPT-User fetches pages a person asks ChatGPT to read. Blocking one does not block the others.
- GPTBot obeys robots.txt. A `User-agent: GPTBot` / `Disallow: /` block keeps your content out of future training runs, but has no effect on whether ChatGPT can cite you in a live answer.
- OpenAI publishes verifiable IP ranges for each agent (`openai.com/gptbot.json`, `searchbot.json`, `chatgpt-user.json`), so you can confirm a request is genuine rather than a spoofed user-agent.
- Blocking GPTBot is a training-data decision, not a visibility decision. If you want AI citations, the agent to keep unblocked is OAI-SearchBot.

### How GPTBot Works

GPTBot is the [automated crawler](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/) OpenAI uses to gather publicly available text from the open web so that content can be considered for training future GPT models. OpenAI introduced it in August 2023, alongside documentation telling site owners exactly how to control it. Mechanically it behaves like any well-behaved search crawler: it requests pages over HTTP, identifies itself with a distinct user-agent, and reads your robots.txt before fetching.

The user-agent is the key to recognizing it. GPTBot’s requests carry a token containing the string `GPTBot` and a pointer back to `https://openai.com/gptbot` — for instance, `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot`. Because user-agents can be forged, OpenAI also publishes the crawler’s IP ranges at `openai.com/gptbot.json`, so a server can confirm that a request claiming to be GPTBot actually originates from OpenAI’s infrastructure.

Two things GPTBot does *not* do are worth stating plainly, because most of the confusion around it lives here. GPTBot does not fetch pages to answer a live user question, and it does not build the index that ChatGPT searches. Its only job is collecting content that may be used to train models. That single-purpose scope is why a robots.txt rule aimed at GPTBot changes what future models learn from you, but changes nothing about how the current ChatGPT retrieves and cites you. If you want to shape what AI systems can retrieve rather than what they train on, you are looking at a different layer — the same layer addressed by an [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/) file and by keeping the retrieval-facing agents unblocked.

### GPTBot vs OAI-SearchBot vs ChatGPT-User

OpenAI operates three separate agents, each with its own user-agent, its own purpose, and its own robots.txt controls. Blocking one is not blocking all of them, and this is the single most important thing to understand about GPTBot.

| Agent | Purpose | User-agent token | robots.txt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **GPTBot** | Collects content to train OpenAI’s models | `GPTBot` | Obeyed — block to opt out of training |
| **OAI-SearchBot** | Builds the index behind ChatGPT search and citations | `OAI-SearchBot` | Obeyed — allow to stay citable in ChatGPT |
| **ChatGPT-User** | Fetches a specific page when a person asks ChatGPT to read it | `ChatGPT-User` | User-initiated, not automated crawling |

The practical consequence: if your goal is to stop your content from training models while remaining visible in ChatGPT’s answers, you block GPTBot and allow OAI-SearchBot. If you block everything with the word “bot” in it, you also remove yourself from the search index that feeds live answers — the opposite of what most publishers actually want. And ChatGPT-User is different again: it fires only when a human pastes your URL or explicitly asks ChatGPT to open a page, so OpenAI treats it as a user action rather than crawling that determines search eligibility.

### How to Allow or Block GPTBot

GPTBot obeys the Robots Exclusion Protocol, so control lives in the `robots.txt` file at your site root. To block GPTBot entirely, add:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /
```

To keep GPTBot out of just part of the site — say a members area and a checkout flow — disallow only those paths:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Disallow: /members/
Disallow: /checkout/
```

To explicitly allow it, either omit any GPTBot rule (the default is allow) or state it directly:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /
```

The critical detail is that each agent must be named separately. A block on `GPTBot` says nothing about `OAI-SearchBot` or `ChatGPT-User`. If you want to opt out of training but stay in ChatGPT’s search results, your file needs two distinct stanzas — one disallowing GPTBot, one allowing OAI-SearchBot. Give changes time to register: OpenAI notes it can take roughly a day for a robots.txt edit to be reflected on its side.

### Example of GPTBot

Picture a mid-size travel publisher that reads a headline about AI scraping and decides to “block the AI bots.” An engineer adds a broad rule that disallows every user-agent containing “GPT,” reasoning it will catch OpenAI’s crawlers in one stroke. Training traffic from GPTBot does drop to zero, exactly as intended.

Three months later, the marketing team notices the site has disappeared from ChatGPT’s cited sources for the destination guides it used to dominate. A competitor is now the source ChatGPT quotes. The cause is not a ranking change or a content problem — it is the robots.txt rule. The overly broad block also matched `OAI-SearchBot`, the agent responsible for the ChatGPT search index, so the publisher had quietly removed itself from the very system that surfaces live citations.

The fix is to separate the two intentions. The publisher rewrites robots.txt with an explicit GPTBot block (opting out of training) and an explicit OAI-SearchBot allow (opting back into search visibility), then verifies with server logs — cross-checking incoming requests against OpenAI’s published IP ranges — that OAI-SearchBot is once again crawling the guides. Within weeks the destination pages return to ChatGPT’s cited sources, while the training opt-out stays firmly in place.

### The thing people get wrong

The mistake I see most often is a team pasting "block GPTBot" into robots.txt because a blog post told them to "keep AI out," then wondering months later why they have vanished from ChatGPT’s cited sources. Those are two different doors. GPTBot governs whether your words help train the next model; OAI-SearchBot governs whether ChatGPT can find and quote you *today*. Block GPTBot and you are only opting out of training — a defensible choice for a paywalled archive or proprietary research. But if the same rule accidentally scoops up OAI-SearchBot, you have quietly deleted yourself from the search index that feeds live answers. Read your robots.txt agent by agent. "AI crawler" is not one thing, and one line does not control all of it.

The takeaway is that GPTBot is a precise instrument, not a blanket AI switch. It answers exactly one question — *may OpenAI train on this content?* — and every other question about how AI systems find, read, and cite your pages is governed by a different agent with a different name. Manage them individually, verify with IP ranges, and decide the training question on its own merits rather than bundling it with visibility you probably want to keep.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### Does blocking GPTBot remove my site from ChatGPT?

No. GPTBot only collects training data. ChatGPT’s live answers are powered by OAI-SearchBot (the search index) and ChatGPT-User (user-triggered fetches). To stay visible in ChatGPT while opting out of training, block GPTBot but allow OAI-SearchBot.

#### What is the GPTBot user-agent string?

GPTBot identifies itself with a user-agent containing the token GPTBot and the URL [https://openai.com/gptbot](https://openai.com/gptbot) — for example, `Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; GPTBot/1.4; +https://openai.com/gptbot`. OpenAI also publishes its IP ranges at [openai.com/gptbot.json](http://openai.com/gptbot.json) for verification.

#### How do I block GPTBot?

Add two lines to your robots.txt at the site root: `User-agent: GPTBot` followed by `Disallow: /`. GPTBot obeys robots.txt, so this stops it from collecting your content for training. To block only part of the site, disallow specific paths instead.

#### Does GPTBot obey robots.txt?

Yes. GPTBot respects robots.txt directives and OpenAI documents how to allow or disallow it. Note that ChatGPT-User, which fetches a page when a person explicitly asks ChatGPT to read it, is a user-initiated action and is not treated as automated crawling.

### The Bottom Line

GPTBot is the training crawler in OpenAI’s three-agent lineup, and treating it as a single on/off switch for "AI" is how sites accidentally erase themselves from ChatGPT. Decide the training question and the visibility question separately: block GPTBot if you do not want your content in future models, but keep OAI-SearchBot open if you want to be cited in AI answers. Manage each agent by its own name in robots.txt, and verify traffic against OpenAI’s published IP ranges.
